title: Laravel Actuator
description: Sample dashboard for the metrics that nwidart/laravel-actuator serves at /actuator/prometheus. https://nwidart.github.io/laravel-actuator/guides/grafana-dashboard/

panels.title: Requests
panels.description: HTTP requests per second, over the last rate interval. Actuator endpoints are not counted.

panels.title: Server errors
panels.description: Share of the requests of the time range that answered 5xx.

panels.title: p95 request duration
panels.description: 95th percentile of the request duration over the time range.

panels.title: Exceptions
panels.description: Exceptions reported by the application over the time range.

panels.title: Failed attempts
panels.description: Queued job attempts that threw, failed or timed out over the time range.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Cache reads that hit, over the time range, for every store.

panels.title: Versions
panels.description: Laravel and PHP versions of the process that answered the last scrape.

panels.title: Application health
panels.description: laravel_health_overall_status: the status of /actuator/health, read during the scrape. With several instances, the most severe one. Ranked DOWN, OUT_OF_SERVICE, WARNING, UP, UNKNOWN: a custom health.status.order does not change it. Empty until health.metrics is on.

panels.title: Health status, by component
panels.description: laravel_health_status: the status of each health indicator over time, read during the scrape. With several instances, the most severe one. Ranked DOWN, OUT_OF_SERVICE, WARNING, UP, UNKNOWN: a custom health.status.order does not change it. Each scrape runs the indicators unless the health cache holds their results. Empty until health.metrics is on.

targets.expr: max by (component) (laravel_health_status{job=~"$job",status="DOWN"} * 5 or laravel_health_status{job=~"$job",status="OUT_OF_SERVICE"} * 4 or laravel_health_status{job=~"$job",status="WARNING"} * 3 or laravel_health_status{job=~"$job",status="UP"} * 2 or laravel_health_status{job=~"$job",status="UNKNOWN"} * 1)

panels.title: Requests per second, by route
panels.description: http.route is the route template, such as /users/{user}.

panels.title: Responses per second, by status class
Request duration
panels.description: Percentiles are estimated from the histogram buckets (5 ms to 10 s).

targets.expr: label_replace(topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])))), "http_route", "(no route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Routes over the time range
panels.description: Requests that matched no route, such as a 404 on an unknown path, are listed as (no route).

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", error_type!=""}[$__range])) / sum by (http_route) (increase(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job"}[$__range])), "http_route", "(no route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Queries per second, by operation
panels.description: Every process: web requests, queued jobs and commands. Failed queries are not recorded.

panels.title: p95 queries per request, top routes
panels.description: From laravel.db.queries, the queries one request ran. A route high in this list often has an N+1 query. Requests to the actuator routes are not recorded.

targets.expr: topk(10, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(laravel_db_queries_bucket{job=~"$job", http_route!=""}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Transactions per second, by result
panels.description: Outer transactions, from laravel.db.transaction.duration. A rising share of rolled_back means more failed writes.

panels.title: p95 transaction duration
panels.description: From the beginning of an outer transaction to its commit or rollback. Long transactions hold locks.

panels.title: Eloquent models per second, by event
panels.description: From laravel.eloquent.models. retrieved is the number of models hydrated; a jump means a query that loads too many rows.

panels.title: Database server connections
panels.description: Read during the scrape: the client connections open on the server of the default connection, from every client, and its limit. MySQL, MariaDB and PostgreSQL only.

panels.title: Pending migrations
panels.description: Read during the scrape: the migrations that php artisan migrate would run. Above 0 after a deploy, the code expects a schema the database does not have yet.

panels.title: Most retrieved models over the time range
panels.description: Eloquent models hydrated, by class.

panels.title: Jobs dispatched and processed, by queue
panels.description: Processed counts each attempt. Dispatched above processed for a while means the queue grows.

panels.title: Failed attempts, by job
panels.description: error.type is the exception class, "failed", or Illuminate\Queue\TimeoutExceededException.

panels.title: Hit ratio, by store
panels.description: hit / (hit + miss). remember() counts a read, then a write on a miss.

panels.title: Operations per second, by result
panels.description: increment, decrement, flush and locks dispatch no event and are not counted.

panels.title: Tasks over the time range
panels.description: A task is named by its description, or its command without arguments. Tasks skipped by withoutOverlapping() are not recorded.

panels.title: Average task duration, by task
panels.description: Over 10 minute windows, because most tasks run at most once a minute.

panels.title: Exceptions per minute, by class
panels.description: Reported exceptions only: a 404 or a validation failure is not reported.

panels.title: Most reported exceptions over the time range
PHP-FPM workers
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered. Only under PHP-FPM.

panels.title: PHP-FPM saturation
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered. Max children reached means requests waited for a worker: raise pm.max_children or add servers.

panels.title: OPcache memory
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered. Wasted memory grows with each deploy until OPcache restarts.

panels.title: OPcache hit ratio
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered.

panels.title: Cached scripts
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered.

panels.title: Load average (1 minute)
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered. Compare it with the number of CPUs of the server.

panels.title: Disk used
panels.description: Read during the scrape, in the process that answers it: with several servers behind one address, each sample comes from whichever server answered. The disk that holds the application.
